coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: P23
names: P23 -- landscaped plaza and lawn (north of the pavilion, toward Chase Center)
record.summary: A landscaped lawn and plaza north of the Mission Creek Park Pavilion, extending toward the Chase Center roundabout; real landscaped/paved open land per satellite imagery, delineated by this project's owner-directed real-gap-fragment method rather than a surveyed parcel boundary. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P23' among the parcels already managed by the Port of San Francisco (not among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), consistent with it being complete by that date. Name and specific operator not confirmed by any source found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- real landscaped/paved open land per Esri satellite imagery and the street/already-tracked-polygon-bounded gap computation, divided at owner-specified cross-sectional seams rather than a surveyed parcel boundary. Name and operator not confirmed by any source found in this pass. The remaining ~5,785 sqm of the original fragment (the building-hugging plaza strip, the panhandle, and P24's own dropped horns) is deliberately left untracked as its own P-number pending further review.
notes.digitized_from: Real-gap-fragment technique: bbox.difference(street buffer).difference(already-tracked polygons) around the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision / 499 Illinois St / Chase Center area (fragment 2, 19,181.78 sqm raw). The owner reviewed a 3-way width-scan split of that fragment (at its two real cross-sectional waists, lat 37.7658 and 37.76665) and then gave a precise construction: P23 is the north piece (piece2, the lawn wedge by the Chase Center roundabout) with its thin building-hugging 'panhandle' dropped, plus the part of the middle piece (piece1, the plaza) that lies east of the seam where piece2's lawn narrows into that panhandle, extended south.

milestones.text: Reported as the nearly 2-acre 'Mariposa Bayfront Park (P23/P24)', under construction and expected to be completed by the end of 2019

open_questions: The April 2019 SocketSite article names the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park' -- not to be confused with Mariposa Park, OCII's own official P26 per its current open-space page (a separate, larger playground park at Mariposa and Owens streets; see this repo's mission_bay_p26_interchange_wedge record's own open_questions for a related P26 label conflict). Not reconciled here, only noted so the two 'Mariposa'-named places aren't conflated.

No source names this specific lawn/plaza or gives its own construction date beyond the April 2019 under-construction report; the Sept 2023 OCII document only establishes it existed and was already Port-managed by that date, which is an upper bound, not a build date.

It sits adjacent to the Chase Center arena (opened September 2019, per this repo's own record 8722025) and to the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision / 499 Illinois St area, but no source ties this landscaped area's own completion to either project.

Whether OCII's own current numbering scheme still uses 'P23' for exactly this footprint was not independently confirmed -- OCII's current public Mission Bay South open-space page (sfocii.org/projects/mission-bay-south/open-space) does not list a P23 at all among the parcels it names (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6, P26).
